title: Annotatio V §.II Ratiocinative close: Church members who keep essentials — even amid many non-overturning errors — stop before §.IV
pass_a_gloss: And just as those endowed with body and rational soul are counted among humans and thought to be contained in the same human society, even when sometimes both the force and virtue of the rational soul are very slight, and some members of the Body are found much deformed; so those are to be reckoned sharers of the same Ecclesiastical Consociation who keep the essentials of the Christian Church, both Theoretical and Practical, though they wrestle with errors and sins alike that do not overturn the Christian Religion — even with a good many of them.
pass_b_english: Just as people with a body and a rational soul still count as human and as members of one society — even when the soul’s force is weak and some bodily members are badly misshapen —
so those who keep the church’s essentials, theoretical and practical, should be counted sharers in the same church Consociation,
even while they wrestle with many errors and sins that do not overturn the Christian religion.
Stop before §. IV (consensus and Consociation judged from the same fundamental principle).
source_text: Sicuti verò hominibus accensentur & societate humana eâdem contineri putantur, qui corpore & animâ rationali praediti sunt, licèt quandoque & animae rationalis vis virtusque exigua perquam, & Corporis membra nonnulla multum deformata inveniantur; ita ejusdem Consociationis Ecclesiasticae participes aestimandi, qui Ecclesiae Christianae essentialia, tàm Theoretica, quam Practica servant, licèt cum erroribus pariter atque peccatis Christianam Religionem haud evertentibus, etiam benè multis, colluctentur.

lemmas.note: errors/sins that do not destroy the religion

notes: Human-society analogy; keep essentials amid non-overturning faults; stop before §.IV.
